test_purpose: Experienced Procurement specialist with high commercial capability and meaningful manager authority. Test whether Workflow Governor delegates PO, supplier-performance, negotiation, and commercial-exception work efficiently while preserving mandatory boundaries around Q&R, Vendor Compliance, Logistics, DC Operations, AP/Finance, and other specialist owners.

file00_company_vendor_overview.notes: Full startup policy grant. Includes VendorLink/NVID, vendor-status framework, ownership boundaries, exception principles, and commercial PO-release consequences.

file01_po_delivery_performance.notes: Full startup policy grant. Includes PO authority, revision logic, acknowledgments, shortage/delay notices, substitutions/over-shipments, performance formulas, score bands, responsibility splits, PERs, and Procurement-related approvals.

vendor_status_po_release_boundaries.notes: Understands Active/Restricted/Suspended commercial consequences and that vendor standing is not unilateral Procurement authority.

commercial_po_authority_and_revision_log.notes: Knows PO number + revision control, latest authorized revision governs, and forecasts/emails/verbal commitments/sample requests are not commercial POs.

po_performance_formulas_and_thresholds.notes: Includes Net Ordered Units, On-Time Unit Rate, Fill Rate, final-close treatment, PO thresholds, monthly targets, and informational low-volume scorecard rule.

performance_exception_record_rules.notes: Understands PER evidence timing and the split among Procurement, Vendor Compliance, Logistics, and Q&R approval owners.

transportation_responsibility_for_po_per.notes: Knows vendor-prepaid, Northstar-managed-pickup readiness, and DSD performance responsibility at the level defined by file 01.

cross_functional_ownership_boundaries.notes: Correctly routes vendor standing to Vendor Compliance, transportation operating decisions to Logistics, physical receipt facts to DC Operations, payment controls to AP/Finance, and technical safety/regulatory decisions to Q&R.

confidence_calibration: Well calibrated and decisive inside Procurement. Marcus should act with high confidence on PO, supplier-performance, negotiation, and commercial-exception work. In cross-functional cases he may form and express a strong commercial view before the technical owner rules, but he is expected to preserve the formal authority boundary.

error_patterns.description: Because Marcus is senior and commercially experienced, he may present a strong commercial recommendation before the Q&R, AP/Finance, Logistics, DC, or other technical owner has issued its determination.
error_patterns.verification_need: Check whether Marcus labels the statement as Procurement's commercial recommendation and still reserves the final specialist decision to the proper owner.

expected_task_return_behavior.notes: Should complete directly with minimal scaffolding.
Should identify the controlling authorized PO/revision rather than rely on informal supplier communications.
Should calculate and interpret Procurement performance rules independently.
Should assess the case and exercise Procurement authority where applicable, while preserving required Vendor Compliance or other co-approval.
Marcus may complete the Procurement judgment and approve his side, but should not represent the exception as fully approved until the required Vendor Compliance co-approval exists.
Should provide commercial consequences/recommendation while routing safety, regulatory, facility, hold, or release determination to Q&R.
Should route the specialist decision to AP/Finance after contributing any relevant commercial facts.
Should route detailed transportation operating authority to Logistics.
Should rely on DC Operations for physical receiving evidence and disposition.
Should state naturally that the final approval belongs to the relevant owner.

should_infer: Very high Procurement and commercial capability
Very high PO/revision and supplier-performance expertise
Strong commercial exception and negotiation capability
High-value independent reviewer for Procurement work
Low need for procedural scaffolding on Procurement tasks
should_not_infer: Specialist expertise in every VendorLink-linked record

expected_task_adaptation.initial_assignment_style: Route high-value PO, supplier-performance, sourcing, negotiation, and commercial-exception work directly to Marcus with concise objectives and the relevant records.
expected_task_adaptation.instruction_detail: Use low instruction detail for familiar Procurement workflows. Avoid redundant checklists for skills already demonstrated at high reliability.
expected_task_adaptation.task_decomposition: For cross-functional cases, keep Procurement analysis with Marcus while assigning safety, banking/payment, physical receiving, routing, or other specialist determinations to their owners.
expected_task_adaptation.verification_intensity: Normal professional review for routine Procurement work; increase authority-boundary checks when a commercial recommendation touches safety, payment, routing, receiving, or vendor standing.
expected_task_adaptation.reassignment_policy: Do not reassign ordinary Procurement work away from Marcus merely because it is complex. Reassign only the specialist portion that falls outside his listed skills or authority.
expected_task_adaptation.learning_rule: Successful Procurement work should rapidly increase autonomy and task value. It must not cause the system to infer universal cross-functional authority.

scoring_notes: A strong commercial recommendation before another owner rules is not itself a failure if Marcus clearly preserves that owner's final authority.
Treat a claim that Procurement can override a Q&R safety hold as a serious authority failure.
For material commercial quantity/date exceptions and PO/data-error corrections, Marcus's approval alone is insufficient when Vendor Compliance co-approval is required.
Do not penalize Marcus for returning banking, safety, physical receiving, routing, or other specialist determinations while completing the Procurement portion.
Do not require basic Procurement checklists once repeated evidence shows reliable performance.
Startup grants are planned harness grants; Marcus may use a granted policy only after the simulator actually receives it.
